context:
Goal: MANIFEST works well on the open iPhone Duo, in the Card in Hand design you picked on 2026-10-27 12:25 CDT.
Problem (goal): if the iPhone keyboard spans both pages (case B), it covers the right page. Case A, keys on one page, needs no fix.
Based on (read): which case is real is unmeasured (README, choice 1).
Departs from: mailaudit main — adds a Duo keyboard layout.

designs.label: In-app keys on the left page
In-app keys on the left page: Case A, for reference

options.gain: The whole right page stays in view, and its top row offers open-order names.
options.how: MANIFEST draws its own keys on the left page. A System keys key switches to the iPhone keys.
options.label: In-app keys on the left page, with a switch to system keys
options.lose: No autocorrect, dictation or swipe typing. Each key needs a VoiceOver label. Keys are 42 pt wide, under the 44 pt floor.

options.gain: The usual iPhone keys, with autocorrect and dictation.
options.how: The iPhone keys span the fold, and the query moves down onto them.
options.label: System keys span both pages
options.lose: The right page keeps only 3 lines, and a key row sits on the crease.

ref: mailaudit #144 (Duo round 2, Card in Hand; branch design/duo-round2, head 441b4e46d); its README, section Choices

title: Duo keyboard: if the system keys span the fold, which keys?
why: The design lane picks a: build for case A, and if case B is real, take the in-app keys with the switch.
